title: Aphelion curation workflow and filter pass
content:
Aphelion stayed in curation mode today, but the work was less about adding another large system and more about making the existing admin surface feel practical for real image review. The goal was to keep the queue, image, metadata, and navigation on one working screen while reducing extra motion, extra save steps, and layout experiments that pulled attention away from the cards themselves.

What changed:

  • Workflow-first admin layout: the curation page was tightened back toward the earlier working composition. The image stage, identity editor, and queue now behave more like one coordinated instrument instead of a wide experiment with too many competing panels.
  • Live metadata editing: the heavier save-button workflow was replaced by lighter field-level saving. Title, description, rarity, series, and attributes now save in place and briefly show a soft saved-state cue beside the field label instead of forcing repeated manual save clicks.
  • Smarter filter popups: With Rarity, With Series, and With Attributes now open translucent multi-select popups with checkbox-style picks, outside-click dismissal, and a reset row. Active selections also replace the header text so the filter state stays legible without opening the menu again.
  • Series and attribute handling got more realistic: cards can now carry more than one series, series and attributes can be added directly from the editor like tag entry, and deleting an attribute from the library now warns with the number of affected images before removal.
  • Queue and shell cleanup: the direct image URL now uses the compact copy icon treatment, the full image can open in a quick overlay and close with click-anywhere or Escape, the queue/footer spacing was corrected so the list stays above the banner, and the public/highlights/admin shell is now visually more consistent.

What did not work as well:

  • The wider folder-browser composition: moving too much folder navigation into the main editing field made the page harder to use, even when the logic itself was sound.
  • Overloaded primary editing controls: keeping too many secondary tools, review toggles, and library-management affordances inside the main identity pane made curation feel heavier than it needed to be.
  • Static one-choice series logic: a single-series assumption stopped making sense once the real collection workflow started asking for more flexible classification.

This was a good refinement checkpoint because it kept the stronger data logic from the earlier reset, but brought the actual editing experience closer to the way the library will really be curated card by card.
